signals.title: @OpenAI: Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet
signals.content: Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications. On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments. While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software. After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely. https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

signals.title: @NATO_ACT: Industry is essential to NATO’s ability to adapt & adopt at the speed of technological change. Getting technology into the hands of Allied f
signals.content: Industry is essential to NATO’s ability to adapt & adopt at the speed of technological change. Getting technology into the hands of Allied forces requires practical cooperation among military operators, national leadership, and industry to build interoperable systems that deploy at scale. In Latvia, nearly 100 defence companies from more than 20 nations are putting their technologies to the test against real operational challenges as NATO Allied Command Transformation leads three major experimentation initiatives: Digital Backbone eXperimentation (DiBaX), the Layered Counter-UAS Initiative (LCI-X), and Next Generation Targeting (NGT). As an integral part of these experiments, industry teams are working alongside Allied operators to test and refine capabilities in realistic, contested environments. This structure gives commercial partners immediate field feedback while giving NATO clear data on what holds up under pressure, what requires refinement, and what is ready for field deployment. Across the Alliance, NATO Allied Command Transformation is tightening the link between warfighting requirements, commercial tech, testing, and actual procurement pipelines. #WeAreNATO #DefenceIndustry #Innovation #Technology
